analysis:
Examined both CLI-reference excerpts and the complete changed-range map. The substantive visible addition is docs/provider/cli-reference.md:905-932: add-on status/hold/release via an owner-only, live-process-bound lifecycle mailbox, with separate socket IPC for add-ons. Holds close admission, drain accepted work for up to 120 seconds and unload models; release normally respects the machine lock, while explicit --force permits serving alongside running VMs. This creates a local resource-coordination contract relevant to TB-003, TB-007, A-001, T-010 and T-028, but the documentation alone establishes no unauthorized access, plaintext exposure or shutdown regression. The deliberate force override is not evidence of an authorization bypass.
Surrounding text retains bounded lifecycle drains and coordinator acknowledgement, fresh restart authorization, issuer-bound logout/revocation, verified model inventory, and encrypted-cache diagnostics; these sections are unchanged in the supplied range map and are not new findings. No supplied change alters encryption, attestation grants or billing directly.
Integration must examine provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/AddonCommand.swift and ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift (referenced at documentation lines 930-932), plus the linked socket contract: verify caller authorization and process binding, lease expiry/disconnect recovery, handling of work still active at the 120-second limit, native owner retirement before memory handoff, and whether same-connection release preserves current authorization rather than reopening after expiry/revocation (T-053). Determine whether the threat model needs an explicit add-on/VM boundary. Implementations are outside these units; claimed controls are unverified contracts, not observed missing controls.
